subject: the #794 staleness half of `worktree_clean`, under a rebase that reapplies identical content
question: Can the artifact-vs-sources mtime comparison report a binary stale when the binary is exactly what those sources produce?

host.note: Logic WAS driven — the readings come from live_534_goto_position runs — but what is measured here is the evidence document's own artifact block, not Logic.

reverify.expected: REVERIFY PASS: touching a Sources file without changing its content leaves `swift build -c release` with nothing to relink, so the binary's mtime stays behind the source's
reverify.cost: offline, no Logic; one release build

method: Read the artifact block of a failing evidence document, then compare the release binary's mtime against every `git ls-files Sources` entry to find which file was newer and why.

observations.quoted: [live_534_goto_position] worktree_clean=False — the evidence describes a build that did not match the tree, or a document too old to say

observations.what: the artifact block that produced it
the tree at the moment of the refusal
observations.note: so the dirty half was not the cause; the staleness half was

observations.cause: a rebase onto main replayed the same commit

observations.what: why the build did not correct it
observations.observed: `swift build -c release` reported Build complete! (82.23s) and left the binary at 18:24
observations.reason: SwiftPM decides by content, and the content was identical, so there was nothing to relink

conclusion: The staleness half of `worktree_clean` is an mtime comparison, and a rebase that reapplies identical content moves source mtimes without changing content. SwiftPM then relinks nothing, so a binary that IS exactly what those sources produce reads as older than them and the live gate refuses a truthful document. The refusal is conservative rather than wrong — it cannot tell this case from a real stale build — but in this repository rebasing is constant, so it will recur on every branch that touches Sources and is rebased before its harness runs.
limits: This is one occurrence. Whether every rebase produces it was not measured; it needs the source mtime to land after the last relink, which a rebase does only when it rewrites a file the branch touches.
It says nothing about the dirty half of `worktree_clean`, which was clean throughout and was not exercised.

The remedy measured here is a forced relink. Whether the check could distinguish this case — by comparing content hashes rather than mtimes — was not attempted, and `touch` is deliberately not a remedy because it asserts a build that did not happen.
`built_from_is_measured: False` was already false before and after, so nothing here says whether that field would have caught anything.
